methodological_questions: Does coverage vary across lineups within a team-season beyond what roster composition mechanically implies?
Is coverage separable from talent and from raw counts of role-holders (collinearity, mechanical coupling)?
Does the talent control behave: non-degenerate, stable across specifications, not outcome-derived, not collinear with coverage?
Are role labels reliable and defined independently of the outcome and of the lineups they are used to classify?
Is power adequate with 90 team-seasons and 420,993 possessions, given the correlated lineup and possession structure?

historical_evidence.finding: Adaptation quality vs talent as a predictor of series wins: corr(talent, adapt)=+0.124. After talent control the adaptation coefficient was p=0.275 (cluster p=0.245). The record states that n~55 series cannot separate coaching adaptation from roster quality.
Series-level AVOID share vs winning: the game-level association is inflated by team-quality confounding, and the series-level association (n=50, p=0.07) is underpowered (~80 series stated as needed).
Play-type label backfill verification: final FAIL. 2024-25 PULL_UP shares are ~0-2% for many teams, team identity checks fail, and 82.8% of PNR labels are proxy_calibrated.
Play-type label audit: overall FAIL (OTHER 20.2%, 40.8% low confidence, foul possessions leak into OTHER, team identity checks fail). The record says label issues undermine downstream findings.
Inferred defensive-scheme labels cannot separate real change from label noise (near-uniform transition matrices).

The A1 adaptation falsification tests (asymmetry, confidence, carryover) indicated that the apparent adapter lift was an artifact. The record lists label error and selection/regression to the mean as limits.
Persistent Impact Score gate: flat, non-decaying lifts collapse under a within-team baseline (team-quality confound). Cohen d~0.01-0.03 despite p~0 from n>150k.
Defensive assignment network modularity was below a volume-schedule null (z=-46.85, powered null). The record says not to lean on topology beyond volume.

Pilot (8 team-seasons) gate: the play-type co-initiation association matrix cleared a fixed-margin null, was team-persistent across split halves, and was not collinear with play-type rates (R2=0.080).
Player-level initiator BEST-AVOID gap was positive, but only 3 players cleared n>=30 in both tiers. The record limits it by small sample.
Star-suppression lineup cells were described without placebo or matching. The record says later work treated similar gaps as artifacts.

evidence_establishes: No retrieved record tests organizer/shaper/terminal lineup coverage directly, so no earlier answer to this question was found.
The project's play-type labels were recorded as failing audits (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014), so any role label built on them is a recorded risk.
Earlier attempts to separate a behavioural construct from talent with ~50-55 series units were recorded as underpowered or confounded (FAM:SF-APPS-027, FAM:SF-CHT-039).
Pooled possession-level effects with large n were recorded to collapse under within-team baselines (FAM:SF-CHT-029).
A fixed-margin-null, split-half, collinearity-checked gate design passed in an 8-team pilot (FAM:SF-PAP-001), a template for the design but not evidence about coverage.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether lineup coverage varies within team-seasons beyond roster mechanics.
Whether coverage is separable from talent or role counts.
How a talent control would behave here, since no record tested one on lineup-level units.
Whether organizer, shaper and terminal roles can be labelled reliably; none of the returned records defines these roles.
Anything about the 2025-26 data; all retrieved records relate to earlier data or other questions.
own_inferences: The question bundles three sub-claims (variation, separability, control behaviour) that should be pre-registered as separate gates with their own pass/fail thresholds.

Within-team variation in coverage is close to guaranteed whenever substitutions vary the five on court, so a bare 'it varies' test is nearly trivial. The informative test is variation relative to a null that reshuffles lineups given the roster and minutes.

Separability from role counts is partly mechanical: coverage (>=1 of each role) is a deterministic function of which role-holders are on court. Separability must therefore be defined as incremental information beyond the count vector, for example the proportion of coverage variance not explained by counts, or the incremental effect on a lineup outcome.
The unit that gives power is the lineup stint within a team-season. The 90 team-seasons is a cluster count and bounds precision for any team-level claim.

Role labels defined from outcome-linked quantities (points scored for terminal, assists for organizer) would build in an association with efficiency. Roles should be defined from non-outcome actions (initiation, ball-handling and shot-creation frequency) on a separate sample, preferably prior-season or odd-game data.

Talent control is likely to misbehave if it is lineup net rating or on-court plus-minus, because that is outcome-derived and collinear with coverage. Use player priors from other seasons or box-score-based talent measured in disjoint games.
Because the question is a measurement gate rather than a causal claim, a clearly specified version is likely to give a determinate answer, but the risk of artifact from labels is substantial.
uncertainties: Role definitions (organizer, shaper, terminal) and thresholds are not given in the task, and no retrieved record defines them.
The quality of the initiator field in the graph database is unknown; play-type labels failed past audits, and it is unknown whether that failure applies to the initiator field.
The 90 team-seasons count presumably covers 2022-23 to 2025-26 with partial 2025-26 data; whether playoffs are included is unspecified.
The meaning of 'talent control behaves' is not specified (sign, stability, collinearity thresholds); this must be fixed before analysis.
Whether 'separable' means statistical separability or predictive incremental value is not stated.

historical_effect.explanation: No retrieved record answers the question, so the historical evidence did not decide it. It did change the design and the decision to 'proceed_with_changes': failed label audits (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014) require a label-reliability gate and non-outcome role definitions, FAM:SF-CHT-029 shows pooled effects collapsing without within-team baselines, and FAM:SF-APPS-027 and FAM:SF-CHT-039 show talent confounding at small n, so inference runs at lineup level with cluster-aware inference and an external talent measure.

blocking_constraints.text: Role labels depend on initiator and play-type derivation whose earlier audits failed; if the role-label reliability gate fails, the question is untestable with this data.
Coverage is a deterministic function of role counts on court, so 'separable from counts' needs a null that conditions on roster counts, otherwise the answer is trivially no.

prior_work.summary: No retrieved record tests lineup role coverage. Related records bear on the measurement and confounding problems (label failures, talent confounding at small n, within-team baselines), and one (FAM:SF-PAP-001) offers a gate-design template. They do not answer this question.

risks.text: Role labels derived from inferred play types and initiators may be noisy; earlier audits failed (FAM:SF-APPA-030, FAM:SF-APPM-014). Misclassification would distort coverage and could produce spurious variation.
If roles are defined from points, assists or efficiency, coverage will correlate with outcomes by construction. Define roles from non-outcome action frequencies.
Coverage is a function of which role-holders are on court; variation and 'separability' are partly mechanical and need a roster-conditioned null.

Coverage is correlated with lineup talent, minutes, starters vs bench, opponent and garbage time (FAM:SF-CHT-029, FAM:SF-APPS-027). Use within-team-season comparisons, with controls for opponent, score state and stint length.
Role labels and talent estimated on the same games as the outcome leak information. Estimate them on disjoint games (prior season or odd/even split).
Only 90 team-seasons; many lineups are sparse. Lineups with few possessions yield noisy coverage and outcome estimates, and the 2025-26 data may be partial.
Lineups missing one role (low coverage) may be rare within some team-seasons, leaving little within-team contrast.
Role identity of each player may be unstable across seasons and teams, and a talent measure may be weakly reliable; test split-half reliability.
Three roles, several talent specifications, seasons and regular-season/playoff splits give many comparisons; the gates and primary tests must be pre-specified.
League play-style and labelling quality vary by season (e.g., 2024-25 PULL_UP label collapse in FAM:SF-APPA-030); check season stability.

design.estimand: Three pre-registered gates. G1 (label reliability): split-half and cross-season stability of role assignment for players (e.g., Cohen's kappa or rank correlation >=0.6), and agreement with an independent box-score proxy. G2 (within-team variation): the share of coverage variance that lies within team-season, compared with a roster-conditioned permutation null that shuffles lineup composition given each team's player minutes and role counts. G3 (separability and talent control): the incremental value of the coverage indicator (and its three components) for lineup-stint offensive efficiency beyond role counts and an external talent measure, plus the correlation of coverage with the talent control (collinearity VIF<5) and stability of the talent coefficient sign/size across specifications.
design.unit: Lineup stint (five-player unit within a game, from substitution intervals) nested in team-season; team-season is the cluster for inference. Possession is the outcome observation, aggregated to stint.
design.sample: 2022-23 through 2024-25 regular seasons as the primary confirmatory sample, with 2025-26 regular season (complete) as holdout. Playoffs analysed separately and flagged exploratory. Exclude garbage-time possessions and lineups below a pre-set minimum of possessions (e.g., >=50 pooled over the season, fixed before data inspection); report how many team-seasons and lineups survive.
design.power: Report the effective number of lineups per team-season and compute a minimum detectable effect by simulation with team-season cluster bootstrap before analysis. The G2 and collinearity checks have ample power at lineup level; G3 incremental-value claims are limited by 90 clusters and must be stated as an MDE, not as 420,993 independent observations. If the MDE for the outcome effect exceeds a plausible effect (~0.02-0.03 PPP), label G3 outcome claims as untestable and report only the G1-G2 results.
design.controls: Role labels and talent are estimated on disjoint data (prior-season or odd games), not the outcome games. Talent control = external player prior (e.g., prior-season box-score-based rating or minutes-weighted prior), not on-court net rating. Include team-season fixed effects, opponent strength, score state/period, stint length, home/away and number of role-holders (counts) as covariates. Roles defined from non-outcome action frequencies (initiation share, creation for others, finishing share), thresholds fixed in advance.
design.falsification: (1) Placebo: permute role labels across players within team-season, preserving counts, and require that real coverage effects exceed the permutation distribution. (2) Shuffle lineup compositions within team given player minutes, to test G2. (3) Negative control outcome: coverage should not predict a pre-lineup quantity such as the opponent's prior-season strength. (4) Re-run with a coarser alternative role definition and with the 2025-26 holdout; require the same sign. (5) If the role labels fail G1, stop and report untestable.
design.multiplicity: One primary test per gate (G2 pooled variation; G3 joint coverage indicator incremental value). Component-level (organizer, shaper, terminal), season-level and playoff results are secondary, with Holm correction across the 3 components and descriptive reporting for seasons.
design.decision_rule: Proceed to G2 only if G1 passes. Support the claim only if: G1 passes; G2 observed within-team variation exceeds the roster-conditioned null (p<0.01 by permutation) with a substantively non-trivial excess; and in G3 coverage retains a non-zero incremental effect (CI excluding zero by team-season cluster bootstrap) beyond counts and talent, with talent VIF<5 and talent coefficient sign/size stable across specifications. Reject if the CI for coverage is within a pre-set equivalence bound (e.g., ±0.01 PPP) and the MDE is below that bound. Otherwise classify as untestable or uncertain.
design.data_version: NBA per-game play-by-play, substitution rotation intervals, starters and box-score summaries, plus graph database possession records, as available on 2026-07-13: 2022-23 to 2024-25 regular season and playoffs, 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21). Freeze the data snapshot, label code and thresholds before any outcome is examined.

You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.
